Most services expose something like `/comments` or `/domains/{domain}/comments`. | `https://api.example.com/comments?domain=apple.com` | `url = "https://api.example.com/comments"` | | 2 | **Add the `delta_key`** for authentication. Common patterns:
• Header: `Authorization: Bearer `
• Query param: `?delta_key=`
• Custom header: `X-Delta-Key: ` | `-H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_DELTA_KEY"` | `headers = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {YOUR_DELTA_KEY}"}` | | 3 | **Send the request** and parse the JSON response. | `curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_DELTA_KEY" "https://api.example.com/comments?domain=apple.com"` | ```python
import requests
response = requests.get(url, headers=headers, params={"domain": "apple.com"})
data = response.json()
``` | | 4 | **Handle errors** – check `response.status_code` and look for error messages in the body. | `curl -i ...` | `if response.status_code != 200: print(response.text)` | ### Full cURL example ```bash curl -s \ -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_DELTA_KEY" \ "https://api.example.com/comments?domain=apple.com" ``` ### Full Python example ```python import requests API_URL = "https://api.example.com/comments" DELTA_KEY = "YOUR_DELTA_KEY" headers = { "Authorization": f"Bearer {DELTA_KEY}", # If the API expects a different header, replace the key above. } params = { "domain": "apple.com", # Add any other required query parameters here. } response = requests.get(API_URL, headers=headers, params=params) if response.ok: comments = response.json() print(comments) else: print(f"Error {response.status_code}: {response.text}") ``` ### Things to double‑check 1. **Endpoint URL** – Verify the exact path (`/comments`, `/domains/apple.com/comments`, etc.) in the API docs. 2. **Authentication scheme** – Some APIs use `X-Delta-Key` instead of `Authorization`. 3. **Rate limits** – If you’re making many requests, watch for `429 Too Many Requests`. 4. **Response format** – The API may return a list of comment objects; inspect the schema to know which fields you need. Once you have the comments, you can iterate over them, filter by date, sentiment, or any other criteria your application requires. Happy coding!
